$comment: Agents may only change the 'passes' field, and only after verification with make check. Humans add and edit items. Items F-001..F-022 were added on 2026-11-13 at the owner's request from docs/PLAN.md section 9 (milestones M0-M2). One item per session; 'depends_on' lists items that must pass first; 'needs_device' means the item needs Jakub's machine with a signed-in CLI (not the cloud container).

features.title: Bootstrap the repository for Tauri 2 + Rust core + React/TypeScript UI
acceptance: Every TODO(bootstrap) in AGENTS.md, memory/project-context.md, docs/architecture.md and the Makefile is replaced with the stack from docs/PLAN.md (grep for TODO(bootstrap) outside excluded dirs returns nothing)
A Tauri 2 app scaffold exists with a Rust core crate and a React + TypeScript + Vite UI
make setup, make lint (cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy -D warnings, tsc --noEmit, eslint) and make test (cargo test, vitest) run and pass
At least one Rust unit test and one UI unit test exist and pass
CI installs the Rust and Node toolchains and runs make check on ubuntu-latest
ADRs 0002 (Tauri 2 + Rust core), 0003 (SQLite per profile) and 0004 (drive official CLIs, no API keys) are written from docs/PLAN.md

features.title: CI builds installers for macOS, Windows and Linux
acceptance: A GitHub Actions matrix (macos-latest, windows-latest, ubuntu-latest) runs make check and tauri build
Unsigned installers (dmg, msi or nsis, AppImage and deb) are uploaded as workflow artifacts
The workflow runs on pull requests and on main

features.title: Core storage: app DB and per-profile SQLite with forward-only migrations
acceptance: SQLite opened in WAL mode; app DB and one DB per profile under the local app data directory
Forward-only numbered migrations tracked in PRAGMA user_version
The database is copied before a migration runs
An older schema version opening a newer database refuses with a clear error (tested)
Tests use a temporary directory, no real user data

features.title: Typed IPC and event channel between Rust core and UI
acceptance: TypeScript types for commands and events are generated from the Rust definitions and checked in CI (stale types fail make lint)
A sample command and a sample streamed event are covered by a Rust test and a UI test
Tauri capabilities expose only the commands the main window needs; no generic run-command or read-file IPC
A strict Content Security Policy without inline scripts is configured

features.title: UI shell and design system (layout similar to the Claude desktop app, own branding)
acceptance: Design tokens (colour, spacing, radius, typography) as CSS custom properties with light and dark themes following the OS
Components: Sidebar (collapsible), TreeItem, MessageItem, ToolCallCard, ApprovalCard, Composer, side Panel, CommandPalette (Ctrl/Cmd+K)
App shell: left sidebar with profile switcher placeholder and navigation, centred main column, resizable right panel
Every component has loading, empty, error and disabled states where applicable
Keyboard operable with visible focus; axe or equivalent accessibility check passes with no serious violations; text contrast at least 4.5:1
No Anthropic logos, icons, fonts or trademarks are used
Screenshots of light and dark themes at desktop width are attached to the PR

features.title: Spike: drive claude -p stream-json from Rust with a subscription login
acceptance: A Rust spike binary starts claude -p with --input-format and --output-format stream-json, a non-default CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and an allowlisted environment, and prints normalised events
The run uses a claude.ai subscription login (claude auth status reports authMethod claude.ai and the expected configDirectory)
A permission request arrives through --permission-prompt-tool, is held 5 minutes, then allowed once and denied once
Cancelling mid tool call leaves no surviving child process
The session is resumed by id and continues
--setting-sources user and --strict-mcp-config suppress a repository hook and a repository .mcp.json
Behaviour with an expired login and with a rate limit is recorded
How to keep -p runs non-bare is recorded

All of the above verified on macOS (the owner's machine); the Windows half of the spike runs in CI against the recorded fixtures plus a process-tree and cancel test with a fake CLI, and a live Windows run is scheduled once a Windows machine is available; findings written as ADR 0005; raw streams saved as test fixtures

features.title: Profiles: create, switch, colour, per-profile database
acceptance: Create, rename, recolour and delete profiles; switcher in the sidebar with a keyboard shortcut
Each profile has its own database and profile directory with user-only permissions
Switching profile changes all visible data; no data from another profile is shown (tested)

features.title: Tool registry with Claude Code, gh and gcloud presets and per-profile config homes
acceptance: Registry entries define binary, config variables, login command, status command and variables to keep out
Presets: Claude Code (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR), GitHub CLI (GH_CONFIG_DIR, --insecure-storage), Google Cloud CLI (CLOUDSDK_CONFIG); custom tools can be added
Sign-in opens the system terminal with the profile environment
Status check shows signed in, expired, not installed or unverified per tool and profile

features.title: Environment allowlist and account verification for runs
acceptance: Run environments are built from an allowlist, not by deleting variables
With ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and GH_TOKEN exported in the parent shell, a run still uses the profile login (tested with a fake CLI)
A run whose claude auth status or gh auth status does not match the profile fails with a clear message

features.title: Two-profile isolation test on a real machine
acceptance: Two profiles signed in to different Claude and GitHub accounts on one machine
Signing out of profile A leaves profile B signed in, for Claude Code and gh
gcloud preset passes the same test or is marked unverified in the registry

features.title: Claude Code adapter with launch compilation, event log and live stream
acceptance: Adapter normalises the stream into Vision events using the recorded fixtures from F-006 (replay tests in CI)
Agent definition fields compile to CLI flags as in docs/PLAN.md section 5.3; unsupported fields produce warnings
Events are persisted before the UI shows them; the run view renders messages, tool-call cards and usage live
Model output containing and a javascript: link renders inert (tested)

features.title: Worktree per run with setup command, approvals, cancel, resume and crash recovery
acceptance: Each run gets a worktree on vision/<task-id>/<agent-slug> with the repository setup command and copied files
Permission requests show as approval cards; one allowed and one denied in a test
A pending approval survives 30 minutes
Killing the app mid-run leaves no orphan process; after restart the run is interrupted and Resume continues the same session

features.title: End-to-end: an agent fixes a seeded bug on a subscription login
acceptance: On macOS (live) and in Windows CI (replay), one hard-coded agent fixes a seeded bug in a test repository end to end
Every tool call is visible in the UI, with one human approval
Recorded as a short screen capture attached to the PR
